newsitem.title: INDIA: Higher volumes to help Indian petrochemicals firms.
newsitem.headline: Higher volumes to help Indian petrochemicals firms.

text.p: Indian petrochemicals firms are expected to show higher earnings in fiscal 1997/98 (April-March) from large capacity additions but prices will continue to face pressure, analysts said on Thursday.
Reliance Industries Ltd and state-run Indian Petrochemicals Corporation Ltd (IPCL) are the country's two big petrochemicals firms.
"For Reliance profits growth will basically come from higher volumes, said Sanjeev Prasad, petrochemicals analyst at Kotak Securities Ltd, the Indian associate of Goldman Sachs.
"For 1997/98 we're seeing volumes growth of 134 percent," he said. "Polyester chain products alone will grow 80 percent."

According to a consensus forecast of 18 brokerages and securities firms polled by Reuters, Reliance's net profit is expected to rise 23.9 percent to 8.1 billion rupees in the first half (April-September) of 1997/98 against 2.8 percent growth in the year-ago period.
Analysts said average prices of polyester staple fibre (PSF) and polyester filament yarn (PFY), two products that account for the bulk of Reliance's profits, had fallen this year compared to 1996/97.

The average price of PSF during April-August this year was 48,500 rupees ($1,358) a tonne compared to 58,950 rupees in 1996/97 while PFY prices averaged 68,200 rupees against 73,650 rupees, the analysts said.

Hitesh Bhatia, petrochemicals analyst at First Global Finance, said PSF production in April jumped 89 percent on year-on-year basis and PFY output rose 23 percent, with Reliance contributing to the bulk of the fresh capacity.
Reliance had commissioned huge capacities for several products in the last quarter of fiscal 1996/97.
These included 360,000 tonnes a year polypropylene plant, 120,000 tonne monoethylene glycol, 350,000 tonne purified terephthalic acid, 160,000 tonne PSF and 60,000 tonne polyester fibre plant.

By the end of 1997/98, total volume output is expected to rise to 6.2 million tonnes from 1.6 million tonnes in 1995/96, and expansion projects on hand would take the total capacity to 9.3 million tonnes by 1998/99, analysts said.

"Reliance's average price realisations this year will be 5-7 percent lower than 1996/97," Bhatia said, adding that the firm will have to cut prices to keep market share following huge capacity additions.
Kotak's Prasad said his conservative forecast for Reliance in 1997/98 was a net profit growth of 10.6 percent. "We do not see much improvement in margins," he said.
IPCL, the second largest petrochemicals firm, is projected to see its first half net profit rise 8.6 percent to 2.7 billion rupees, according to the consensus estimate.
Prasad said he expects IPCL's workings to improve in the second half as production stabilises pushing up sales volumes.
